details.context: Three trading days AFTER 2026-02-10 Q4-2025 earnings 8-K; just before 10-K filing (2026-02-20). Open window post-earnings.
Bought ~$492k total across Nov 14 & 17, 2025 — week after Q3 2025 earnings (8-K filed 2025-11-04). Insider-trading window was open.

form4_purchases_code_P.ltip_grants_code_A_derivative: 26 (annual Dec-15 LTIP grants to all NEOs & directors — routine compensation, not signal)
form4_purchases_code_P.interpretation: EXCEPTIONAL Form-4 profile. Zero open-market sales by any insider in 18 months despite -28.8% drawdown. CEO Jordan Kaplan (Chairman) bought 98k shares ($998k) three trading days after Q4-2025 earnings — the largest CEO open-market buy of his tenure. EVP/GC Aronson added ~$492k after Q3 earnings. Director Simon added ~$592k in June 2024. Both C-suite buys were in clear post-earnings windows when material non-public information had just been released. This is the textbook bullish insider-conviction signal: open-market code P, C-suite, sized meaningfully, into drawdown, immediately after public disclosure (not before).

insider_vs_calendar.note: Zero insider sales in 18-month lookback; budget-calendar overlay not applicable to a CA office REIT (no federal-program exposure). Connector run would return NO_PROXIMATE_SALES by construction.

rfm_tuples.R: Office Occupancy Rate as of December 31, 2025 was 78.0% (versus 79.2% 2024, 81.0% 2023, 83.7% 2022, 84.9% 2021). Multifamily Occupancy 98.0% (10-K Item 7).
rfm_tuples.f: Mode-A: confirm stated occupancy against subsequent 10-Q reported numbers (Q1 2026 10-Q filed 2026-05-08).
rfm_tuples.M_value: 10-Q reports March 31, 2026 office occupancy 77.5% (down 50bps QoQ), Q1 2026 average office occupancy 77.7% (down 50bps from 78.2% FY25 avg). Office Leased Rate ticked up 50bps to 80.9%. Multifamily Occupancy 98.1%.
rfm_tuples.interpretation: 10-K disclosed occupancy honestly; subsequent 10-Q shows continued, monotonic deterioration in office occupancy — fifth consecutive year of declines (~700bps since 2021). Trend is consistent and unhidden, but the operational signal is clearly deteriorating. The 50bps QoQ slip with Leased Rate +50bps suggests signed-not-commenced is building but execution is slow. Not a SEVERE disclosure issue — DEI quantifies it cleanly each quarter — but the underlying business is genuinely impaired.

rfm_tuples.R: FY2025 FFO was $295.3M, down $50.2M / -14.5% from $345.5M in 2024. 'Our FFO was adversely impacted by the effects of inflation and higher interest rates during 2025 and 2024.' (10-K MD&A)
rfm_tuples.f: Mode-A: cross-check the -14.5% FFO decline against the components (interest expense + NOI) and against Q1 2026 trajectory.
rfm_tuples.M_value: Interest expense FY25 $266.7M vs FY24 $229.4M (+16.3%); FY25 Same-Property Office NOI $478.2M vs $487.2M (-1.9%); Q1 2026 net (loss) attributable to common -$2.5M (vs +$39.8M Q1 2025) and Q1 EPS -$0.02 vs +$0.24. Interest expense Q1 2026 cash $57.3M vs $57.8M (flat) — net loss driven primarily by absence of $47.2M JV-consolidation gain that boosted Q1 2025.
rfm_tuples.interpretation: FFO declining ~15% per year is real distress, but the issuer discloses drivers cleanly: rising interest expense as swaps roll off (effective rate on fixed/swapped debt only 4.39% currently, vs market 5-6%) and lower office NOI. Q1 2025 vs Q1 2026 comp is distorted by a one-time non-cash gain. Not a Mode-B catch — the issuer is transparent; the business itself is impaired.

rfm_tuples.R: Total / Weighted Average dividend for 2025 was $0.76 per share; '$ 0.19 — — 100.0% — Return of Capital' for each quarter (10-K Note 11 / Dividends unaudited classification).
rfm_tuples.f: Mode-B: GIVEN dividend was held at $0.76/yr through a 14.5% FFO decline, derive coverage ratio — what does retention look like vs CapEx + debt amortization needs?
rfm_tuples.M_source: self_text (10-K & 10-Q cash flow statements + balance sheet)
rfm_tuples.M_value: FY25 dividends paid to common ~$127M (4× $31.8M); FY25 basic EPS $0.09; cash from operations $386.9M vs CapEx $265.3M = $121.6M free cash before refi → dividend roughly fully consumes FCF. 100% of 2025 dividends classified as Return of Capital (not Ordinary Income), confirming there is no taxable REIT income behind them. Dividend was already cut in 2023 from $0.28 to $0.19. Cash on B/S $357M vs $1.18B of 2026 maturities.
rfm_tuples.interpretation: Mode-B catch. The 100% Return-of-Capital tax classification is a quiet, structurally honest tell that current distributions exceed REIT taxable income — the dividend is being funded out of depreciation cushion + asset basis, not earnings. With $1.18B of 2026 maturities, refi expense uncertainty, continued occupancy decline, and FCF approximately equal to dividend obligation, there is meaningful tail-risk of another dividend cut. The issuer is not required to disclose 'dividend at risk' — they meet REIT distribution minimums via Return of Capital — but the structural reality is that the payout is unsupported by current earnings.

rfm_tuples.R: Future Principal Payments: '2026 $ 1,181,987 [thousand]' / four term loans maturing Aug-Nov 2026 totaling $1.18B at SOFR + ~1.20-1.25% (currently floating, no swap, no cap). (10-K Note 8 + 10-Q Note 6)
rfm_tuples.f: Mode-B: derive refinancing risk. GIVEN 21% of total debt rolls in 7-10 months at current market rates and the issuer is in an actively distressed office sector, what is the rate gap?
rfm_tuples.M_source: self_text (10-K debt schedule + interest expense run-rate)
rfm_tuples.M_value: Three large 2026 maturities: $415M (Aug 15), $366M (Sep 19), $400M (Nov 1) at SOFR+~1.25% (currently floating). Weighted average annual interest rate on fixed/swapped portion 4.39% (10-K) / 4.41% (10-Q). New term loans issued Aug 2025 ($941M of Fannie Mae loans) were priced at 4.80% fixed → so refis are inflicting +40-60bps incremental cost. Cash on hand $357M = covers only 30% of 2026 maturity stack.
rfm_tuples.interpretation: Mode-B catch but not SEVERE: the maturity wall is large and refi spread is rising, but DEI demonstrated capability in Aug 2025 ($941M Fannie Mae closing replacing $930M of old loans). Fannie Mae multifamily funding is reliable; office refis are more uncertain. The 2028 maturity stack ($1.31B) is the larger tail risk. Issuer discloses the table fully — not a hidden item — but a 21% rollover at +50bps cost is real interest-expense headwind ahead.

rfm_tuples.R: Top tenant William Morris Endeavor is 2.8% of Annualized Rent; top 5 tenants combined 8.6%; 'a diverse mix of industries' (10-K Item 1).
rfm_tuples.f: Mode-A confirms diversification; Mode-B derives: given strong diversification, what is the lease-expiration cliff in 2026 that issuer doesn't headline?
rfm_tuples.M_source: self_text (10-K In-Service Office Lease Expirations table)
rfm_tuples.M_value: 566 leases expiring in 2026 covering 2,044,738 SF (11.7% of total) representing $94.0M annualized rent (14.6% of total office rent). 2027 expirations are 12.9% of SF / 16.5% of rent. Tenant base is genuinely diverse: top 5 = 8.6%, top tenant 2.8%, 51% of leases < 2,500 SF.
rfm_tuples.interpretation: Mode-A passes cleanly. Tenant diversification is unambiguously strong — no single tenant exposure risk, broad industry mix (legal 19.7%, FS 16.8%, RE 13.3%, healthcare 9.9%). The 2026/2027 expiration cliff is disclosed in standard format. With current Leased Rate 80.9% > Occupancy Rate 77.5%, signed-not-commenced (~422k SF) provides some backfill. Submarket rent gap (current $47.65 PSF vs at-expiration $53.68 PSF in 2026 leases) suggests mark-to-market potential rather than mark-to-market loss.

rfm_tuples.R: 'Impairment losses — —' for FY2025 and FY2024 (10-K NOI reconciliation table); accumulated deficit grew to -$1,539,710 thousand by Q1 2026 (10-Q balance sheet).
rfm_tuples.f: Mode-B: given Gross Investment in Real Estate $12.86B, accumulated D&A $4.13B, net carrying value $8.73B — and given office sector cap-rate expansion has been brutal (peer impairment cycles 2023-2025) — derive whether absence of impairments is credible.
rfm_tuples.M_value: Zero impairment in FY25, FY24, FY23 (per NOI reconciliation). Schedule III shows several wholly-owned properties with encumbrances exceeding book value (e.g. The Landmark Los Angeles $240M encumbrance vs $331M total carrying value but $0 land cost — entirely in 'Cost Capitalized Subsequent'). Sherman Oaks Galleria carries $300M encumbrance on $476.9M gross / $263.5M net carrying value. Construction loan at Wilshire Bundy has 80%+ LTV implied. Accumulated deficit $1.54B is a function of historic GAAP losses & dividends-in-excess-of-earnings, not necessarily an impairment trigger.
rfm_tuples.interpretation: Mode-B candidate. Zero impairments on $8.7B net real estate during a brutal office cycle (peers SLG, VNO, BXP, KRC have all recorded impairments 2023-2025) is suspicious. However, DEI's portfolio is highly concentrated in 'premier' Westside LA submarkets that have held up better than CBD office, and impairment under ASC 360 is binary (undiscounted-cash-flow test) so even significant fair-value declines don't trigger writedowns if held-for-use. Without third-party appraisal data (cap-rate observable transactions in DEI submarkets), I cannot adjudicate this Mode-A. Flag as UNVERIFIABLE — not a SEVERE call but a watch item.

rfm_tuples.R: 'We had seven holders of record of our common stock on February 13, 2026.' — incidental; the substantive insider-trading signal is in the 26 Form 4 filings filed Jan 2024 - May 2026.
rfm_tuples.f: Form 4 m-source: parse non-derivative transaction codes for all reporting persons since Jan 2024; classify code P (open-market purchase) vs code S (open-market sale) vs code A (grant).
rfm_tuples.M_value: Code-P open-market PURCHASES: 4 transactions, $2.08M aggregate. CEO Jordan Kaplan bought 98,000 sh @ $10.18 on 2026-02-13 ($998k, 3 days post Q4 earnings). EVP/GC Michele Aronson bought 42,126 sh @ ~$11.70 on 2025-11-14 and 2025-11-17 ($492k, week after Q3 earnings). Director William Simon Jr bought 45,000 sh @ $13.15 on 2024-06-10 ($592k). Code-S open-market SALES: ZERO. Code-A grants: 26 LTIP grants on 2024-12-12 & 2025-12-15 (routine annual NEO/director awards, all derivative LTIP units).
rfm_tuples.interpretation: Form 4 evidence STRONGLY supports management commitment. Zero discretionary sales by any insider in 18 months — extraordinary for a public company with >30 reporting persons and ongoing LTIP vesting. CEO Kaplan's $998k open-market buy at $10.18 (near 52-wk low, three trading days after publicly releasing Q4-2025 results = blackout window open) is the highest-quality bullish signal in this framework. C-suite open-market purchases of nearly $1.5M total into the -28.8% drawdown, executed in post-earnings open windows (not blackout-evading insider trades), is the EXACT OPPOSITE of the IONQ/distress-pattern this framework was designed to catch. Per AGENT_PROMPT explicit guidance: 'note this explicitly even if the rest of the disclosure is distressed.'

rfm_tuples.R: 'Repurchases of Equity Securities None.' (10-K Item 5) — no buyback in FY25 despite 28.8% drawdown. Last buyback was 2023: 9.1M shares at $12.03 avg.
rfm_tuples.f: Mode-B: GIVEN insider buying at $10.18 is signaled as undervalued AND there is $357M cash, why is the company not buying back stock?
rfm_tuples.M_value: FY23 repurchase $109.1M / 9.1M shares (avg $12.03). FY24 zero. FY25 zero. Q1 2026 zero. Cash $357M but $1.18B of 2026 debt maturities; the company is preserving cash for refi liquidity, not capital return. Dividends of $127M/yr consume most of FCF.
rfm_tuples.interpretation: Mild tension with DEI-07: if stock is cheap enough for CEO personal buying at $10.18, why not corporate buying? Answer (Mode-B inference): $1.18B 2026 maturity wall + Fannie/CMBS lenders penalize aggressive corporate buybacks. The capital-allocation choice is rational. Note that the 2023 buyback was at $12.03 — current ~$10 is cheaper. The gap between insider personal action (buying) and corporate action (preserving liquidity) is information-consistent: insiders see undervaluation but the entity needs balance-sheet defense. Mild negative on disclosure (not a SEVERE call).

summary: DEI is genuinely distressed (78.0% office occupancy down 700bps from 2021; FFO -14.5% YoY; net loss in Q1 2026; 100% Return-of-Capital dividend tax classification; $1.18B 2026 debt maturity wall) BUT the disclosure quality is high and management has put substantial personal capital on the line. Form-4 evidence is the dominant signal: zero insider sales in 18 months, CEO Jordan Kaplan bought $998k at $10.18 three trading days after Q4-2025 earnings, EVP/GC bought $492k in November post-Q3, director $592k in June 2024 — total $2.08M open-market purchases in 18 months with ZERO sales. Per AGENT_PROMPT guidance for Form 4 evidence: 'open-market code-P purchases by C-suite or directors, sized meaningfully, into drawdown — note this explicitly even if the rest of the disclosure is distressed.' This is the exact opposite of the IONQ short-thesis pattern. The honesty-alpha framework is designed to catch lying-during-distress; DEI is distressed-but-not-lying with strong insider commitment. Verdict: NEUTRAL with LONG bias on the insider signal.
